question: What will be Lake Mead’s elevation at the end of November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Start: Nov 4 daily 1039.29 ft (Oct EOM 1038.85), rising after October storms but decelerating (+0.13, +0.15, +0.08 ft/day). Oct 24-Month Study most-probable expected Oct->Nov change of about -1.3 ft under 6.0 maf Powell release, but it underpredicted October by 3.56 ft because of storm inflow and lower demand. Nov 2025 gained 1.34 ft under a higher 7.48 maf Powell release. Median: a short continued rise, then a slow decline of ~0.04 ft/day, giving ~1038.7. Markets: only Polymarket contracts on minimum elevation through Apr 2027 (different contract, not used as an anchor); no market on November end-of-month found.
calls.dossier:
- USBR end-of-month series (mead-elv.html, read 2026-11-05): 2026 values Jan 1065.37, Feb 1066.14, Mar 1062.05, Apr 1056.32, May 1050.00, Jun 1044.58, Jul 1041.10, Aug 1038.83, Sep 1037.80, Oct 1038.85. 2025 values: Oct 1057.57, Nov 1058.91 (+1.34), Dec 1062.24.
- USBR daily levels (levels.html): Nov 1 1038.93, Nov 2 1039.06, Nov 3 1039.21, Nov 4 1039.29 ft (6,929 kaf content); about 70 kaf per ft at this elevation.
- Record low around Oct 22, 2026 (~1037.2-1037.3); lake up ~2 ft by early Nov after Oct 11 and Oct 22 storms (KTAR; autonocion). Lake Mead basin precipitation was 465% of normal in October; CBRFC October inflow forecast 120 kaf vs 71 kaf in the model.
- Oct 15, 2026 24-Month Study most probable (per autonocion): Oct EOM 1035.29 (actual 1038.85, so 3.56 ft too low), Nov EOM 1033.97 (an Oct->Nov change of -1.32 ft), Dec 31 1034.52. Weekly sheet of Oct 26 still projected Dec 31 at 1034.52.
- Oct 2026 24MS probable-max: Dec 31 1035.36 (western-water.com). Probable-min trace much lower later in 2027.
- Powell WY2027 release set at 6.0 maf, the bottom of the 6-7 maf range (autonocion); WY2025 was 7.48 maf, so Mead inflow is lower than last year.
- Status quo: daily rise is decelerating; drivers of further change are Glen Canyon monthly release, Hoover release (lower demand after rain), and any new storms (El Nino hopes).
- Resolves off the USBR mead-elv.html November 2026 end-of-month value; no re-resolution on revisions.
- Event window: Nov 1 -> Nov 30, 2026 end-of-month value; as of Nov 5 ~13% elapsed.
- Searched but not found: the exact Nov 2026 Glen Canyon and Hoover monthly release volumes; readable text of the Oct 24MS PDF and the Nov weekly update; any mid-November Glen Canyon high-flow experiment.
- Markets: only Polymarket contracts on minimum elevation through Apr 2027 (a different quantity).
calls.reference_class: Lake Mead November end-of-month change vs October end-of-month in recent years (2023-2025), adjusted using the Oct 2026 24-Month Study most-probable Nov change

calls.reasoning: End-Oct official value 1038.85 ft; lake 1039.29 on Nov 4 (+0.44 in 4 days). The Oct 24-Month Study projected an Oct->Nov change of -1.32 ft (1035.29->1033.97), but it was made before October storms that left the lake ~3.6 ft above its forecast, so use its delta, not its level. With Powell releasing 6.0 maf in WY2027 (less than last year, when Nov rose +1.34) and low November demand, the rest of November is likely flat to slightly falling. lakeprojections.com projects 1038.72 for Nov 30. No matching human market: the Polymarket contracts price the minimum elevation through Apr 2027, a different quantity.

calls.reasoning: October 2026 end-of-month was 1038.85 ft (USBR), ~3.5 ft above the Oct 24-Month Study (1035.29) due to record October storms; lake was ~1039.2 on Nov 3 and rising ~0.1 ft/day. The Oct 24MS projected an Oct->Nov drop of 1.32 ft (to 1033.97); Reclamation reportedly says Oct/Nov will end ~3 ft above that study (~1037), while lakeprojections projects 1038.72 for Nov 30. Storm inflow should taper and planned Powell releases are low, so median slightly below current level. Polymarket contracts are on the seasonal minimum through April 2027 — a different contract, used only as context. No escape mass needed: bounds 1029-1043 are far from the plausible range.

calls.reasoning: End-Oct 1038.85; Nov 4 at 1039.29 with the storm-driven rise slowing. The Oct 24MS most-probable run has the lake falling 1.32 ft Oct->Nov under 6.0 maf Powell releases; its level is stale after the October storms (+3.56 ft above it) but its underlying rate of decline still applies. A small further rise and then ~-0.04 ft/day gives ~1038.5. lakeprojections.com says 1038.72; an unverified report that Reclamation expects ~1037 pulls the low tail down. No matching human market: Polymarket only prices the minimum through Apr 2027.
calls.reconciliation: Factual items (Oct EOM 1038.85, early-Nov dailies, the 24MS Nov delta of -1.32, Powell's 6.0 maf release, the tracker's 1038.72) agree across all runs. The only factual dispute I could not settle is Run 3's unverified claim that Reclamation expects Nov ~3 ft above the 24MS (~1037). No web access this run, so I kept it as partial weight on the lower tail. The judgment dispute is how fast November declines once the storm runoff fades. Applying the 24MS daily rate to the remaining ~22 days after a short continued rise gives ~1038.5, slightly below Runs 1 and 2 and above Run 3. I carried forward a width of ~2.6 ft, between the runs' 2-3 ft.
